name: Doga
summary: Mumbai's dog-masked vigilante and Raj Comics' signature antihero: Suraj, a gym-trained orphan who fights organised crime outside the law. Debuted in Curfew (1992).
origin: Suraj was found as a baby in a rubbish dump by the dacoit Halkan Singh, who raised him more like a pet than a child. A cruel childhood left deep scars. He was later taken in by Adrak Chacha, who ran the Lion Gym, and Adrak's brothers trained him: Haldi in martial arts, Dhania in boxing and Kalimirchi in sharpshooting. When goons sent by a rival gym owner killed the family that trained him, Suraj put on a dog mask and became Doga, taking on Mumbai's gangsters outside the law. Comics later bring him face to face with Halkan Singh, now a minister. Doga breaks the law, and the comics show that he does.
powers: Peak strength and stamina from gym training
Expert marksman with a large arsenal

facts.text: Suraj was found as a baby in a rubbish dump by the dacoit Halkan Singh, who raised him like a pet and called him 'dog'; the grown Suraj later puts on a dog mask and takes the name Doga.
His four trainers are named after kitchen spices: Adrak (ginger), Haldi (turmeric), Dhania (coriander) and Kalimirchi (black pepper).

Suraj's trainers were the Khan brothers: Adrak, a former weightlifting champion who owned the Lion Gym, Dhania, a former heavyweight boxing champion, and Kalimirchi, a champion sharpshooter who also knew explosives.
Dhruva refuses to kill and works within the law, while Doga will use lethal force on criminals, so their differing moral codes make them uneasy partners.
Killota, a former gym member, opened a rival gym and had the Khan brothers murdered; Suraj was the only survivor, and he put on the dog mask to hunt Killota's gang.
The first issue of Rakta-Katha (2021) is titled Kachra Peti, which means 'rubbish bin', matching the place where Suraj was found as a baby.
Halkan Singh, the dacoit who raised Suraj, later becomes a minister named Halkat Singh, and Doga eventually takes him down.
Doga's main enemy, Kaal Paheliya, leaves a puzzle at every crime scene.
Only a few people know who is under the dog mask, among them Inspector Cheetah, a retired policeman turned private detective, and Cheetah's sister Monica, who is Doga's love interest.
Each Khan brother ran his own club: Adrak the Lion Gym, Dhania a boxing school called Lion's Den, Haldi a martial-arts club called Lion Occult, and Kalimirchi the shooting institute Lion Aim Club.
Kunal Kapoor, cast as Doga in 2017, called it by far the most ambitious project he had joined, described the hero as dark and angry, and said he would have to learn many martial arts.
Doga first appeared in Raj Comics issue number 395, titled Curfew.
When Anurag Kashyap talked about a Doga film in 2014, he described him as a vigilante killing machine in the style of Marvel's Punisher, but the project was shelved after Bombay Velvet flopped.
Doga has teamed up with Parmanu, Nagraj, Dhruva, Bheriya, Shakti and Inspector Steel, so he is no lone wolf across the Raj Comics universe.
ThePrint describes Doga as a Mumbai vigilante with bright red eyes who takes the law into his own hands to serve justice from the shadows.
A fan quoted by ThePrint says he loved Doga because the hero stays a plain human who fights corruption and terrorists, even when his comics pit him against aliens.
Doga has no powers, only the ability to talk with dogs and get information from them; the rest is martial arts, boxing, huge stamina, high pain tolerance and a large stock of guns and explosives.
Raised among dacoits, the child Suraj saw endless horrors, and Indianetzone says this pushed him toward becoming a sociopath before the Khan brothers gave him a better life.
Raj Comics lore says Halkan Singh used the infant Suraj as protection during a police raid, and that Suraj later escaped his den with a kidnapped girl named Sonu.
Doga debuted in November 1992 and is described as Raj Comics' first, and so far only, antihero among its major characters.
Kalimirchi, the youngest Khan brother, taught Suraj marksmanship and flying as a fighter pilot, while Haldi taught martial arts and Dhania boxing.
Raj Comics has paired Doga with Anthony in the Mard aur Murda series and with Super Indian in Khoon, and gathered him with Bheriya, Nagraj, Dhruva and Parmanu in the Mai Hu Bheriya series.

kidSummary: Doga is a masked vigilante from Raj Comics who hides behind a dog mask. He has no superpowers, only hard training and a talent for talking to dogs. He is a dark, grown-up antihero who breaks the law, so his stories are for older readers more than small children.

story.title: A rough start
story.text: Suraj is found as a baby in a rubbish dump and raised by the dacoit Halkan Singh, who treats him badly.

story.title: The Lion Gym
story.text: Suraj finds a new family at the Lion Gym, where Adrak Chacha and his brothers train him in strength, boxing, martial arts and shooting.

story.title: The mask
story.text: When the gym family is attacked by the henchmen of a rival, Suraj puts on a dog mask and becomes Doga.

story.title: Mumbai's watchdog
story.text: Doga fights organised crime across Mumbai. He uses dogs to find information, but the comics show that he works outside the law.
